_about: The two courses. Each models a public range. plates lists each steel plate: its distance, its width and height in inches, how high its centre stands above the eye at the firing position (riseFt, surveyed, used by the engine and every picture alike) and where it stands sideways (lateralYd, placed by angle as seen from the firing line). altitudeFt is the surveyed height of the firing position above sea level, for the air. firing is where the shooter stands and which way the line of fire runs, on the surveyed ground of data/terrain.json. blurb is the one line home shows about the course.

angeles-sylmar.blurb: Steel every 100 yards from 100 to 600, up a gentle rise.

firing._about: The firing position and the direction of fire on the surveyed ground: the shooter's place under the shelter, in NAD83 / UTM zone 11N metres (the frame of data/terrain.json) and as latitude and longitude; the bearing is degrees from north, clockwise. The picture's camera stands here; every plate is placed from here.

lat.estimate: latitude of the firing position: the long roofed shelter at the south end of the graded floor, read off the NAIP photograph of 2022-05-04 (80 m west and 66 m north of the range's public map position); the direction of fire is square to the roof, up the floor toward the berms

lon.estimate: longitude of the firing position, the same basis

easting.estimate: UTM easting of the firing position, the same basis; read against the photograph's own grid (data/terrain.json, angeles-sylmar.photo)

bearingDeg.estimate: the bearing of fire in degrees from north: square to the shelter's roof as it lies on the photograph of 2022-05-04, and along the graded floor's long sides

source.note: the surveyed height of the ground at the firing position, metres above sea level (NAVD 88), read from data/terrain.json angeles-sylmar.heights (USGS 1 Meter 11 x37y380 CA_LosAngeles_B23, captured 2024-07-01) at the easting and northing above

pictureReady.estimate: the rifle line keeps the plain picture: its surveyed ground is fetched (data/terrain.json) but its own things (the long sand berm, the lane signs, the pipe target frames) are not drawn yet, so the scene would show the canyon course's boards on it
